## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Sekhiya 68 (*Chamā*; "Sitting on the ground") is a training rule found in the *Sekhiya* section of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* within the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. It establishes proper decorum regarding teaching Dhamma, specifically prohibiting a monk from teaching the Dhamma while sitting on the ground to someone seated on a seat, unless that person is ill [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the rule has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral link this rule to the Theravāda Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (*pli-tv-bu-pm-sk68*), the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga and Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha (*pli-tv-bi-vb-sk68*, *pli-tv-bi-pm-sk68*), and the Parivāra for both monks and nuns [SuttaCentral]. Cross-tradition parallels include versions in the Chinese Dharmaguptaka Vinaya for both monks (*lzh-dg-bu-vb-sk88*, *lzh-dg-bu-pm-sk88*, *lzh-dg-bu-pm-2-sk88*) and nuns (*lzh-dg-bi-vb-sk88*, *lzh-dg-bi-pm-sk88*), as well as the Chinese *Upāliparipṛcchā* (*lzh-upp-bu-sk57*) [SuttaCentral]. Computationally, DharmaNexus identifies 101 matching passages across 43 other Pali texts, reflecting heavy formulaic reuse with adjacent Vinaya training rules, particularly neighboring Sekhiya rules such as Sekhiya 64, Sekhiya 66, Sekhiya 63, and Sekhiya 69 [DharmaNexus].
